```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = identical(Sys.getenv("RCEATTLE_EVAL_VIGNETTES"), "true")
)
```

This guide is for people who want to modify Rceattle itself: add a parameter,
a data input, a new selectivity or suitability form, or a likelihood
component. It is not needed to *fit* models, for that, start with the user
articles ([Introduction](introduction.html) and
[Model options and functionality](model-options-and-functionality.html)).

It consolidates and updates the developer notes on the
[GitHub wiki](https://github.com/afsc-assessments/Rceattle/wiki).

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `R/` | The R side, 67 files. The number prefix tracks pipeline order for the `1-` to `6-` chain; everything under `0-` is shared machinery. Every file is listed in [Every file in `R/`, and what it does](#every-file-in-r-and-what-it-does). |
| `src/TMB/` | The C++ TMB template `ceattle.cpp` and its included `.hpp` modules. |
| `tests/testthat/` | Unit and regression tests, grouped by area. |
| `inst/extdata/` | Excel templates, including `meta_data_names.xlsx` (the authoritative column/switch reference). |
| `data/` | Built-in example data lists (`BS2017SS`, `GOA2018SS`, `NorthernRockfish2022`, …). |
| `vignettes/` | User articles; `vignettes/articles/` holds website-only articles like this one. |
| `.github/workflows/` | `R-CMD-check.yaml` and `pkgdown.yaml` CI. |
| `inst/dev/` | Committed developer notes: `TRAPS.md` (verified traps with their measured numbers), `CLEANUP_BACKLOG.md` (the triaged TODO/FIXME markers), `CONTRIBUTOR-EXPERIENCE.md`, `SIMPLIFY-LOG.md`, and per-topic `TODO-*.md` design records. Read the one for your subsystem before changing it. |
| `data-raw/` | Generators for committed artefacts, notably `regenerate_meta_xlsx.R` for `meta_data_names.xlsx`. |
| `tools/verify/` | 22 standalone verification harnesses `/golden-check` does not cover — the optimizer path, array bounds, the MSE draw digests, the simulation recoveries. |
| `.claude/commands/` | The slash commands referenced below (`/golden-check`, `/new-column`, `/verify`, `/ecosystem-sweep`). Each is a markdown file stating the full procedure, usable as a checklist by a person. |

The whole model (observation model, population dynamics, and likelihood) is
a single C++ TMB script, `src/TMB/ceattle.cpp`, which `#include`s a set
of topical `.hpp` modules. `fit_mod()` is the R entry point; it calls a chain
of helpers that build the TMB inputs, optimize, and label the output.

## I want to change X — where do I start?

The question most people arrive with. Find the row, start at the file, and read
its row in [Every file in `R/`](#every-file-in-r-and-what-it-does), which covers
all 67. Where a row names a vignette, read that first — these rows are
orientation, and a recipe is the job.

| I want to … | Start at | Then usually also |
|---|---|---|
| add a **selectivity form** | **`adding-a-selectivity-form.html` — read it first.** It names all the files and the two static tests that catch a half-finished form; this row is orientation, not the job | the dispatch is `switch (sel_case)` in `src/TMB/selectivity.hpp`, **not** `switch (sel_type)` — `sel_case` is derived, and form 13 under a random walk rewrites itself to `-13`. Five files are always touched: `R/0-switches.R` (`sel_map`), `R/0-column_schema.R`, `R/data.R`, `R/1-data_check.R`, `R/3-build_map.R`. Codes 1-9, 11, 13 and 15 are taken; the next free one is 16 |
| add a **likelihood component** | `src/TMB/ceattle.cpp` §13 and the `JnllRow` enum | `R/6-rename_output.R` (row labels) and `.JNLL_ROW_AXIS` in `R/9-profile.R` — all three must agree, and `test-schema-jnll-rows.R` checks it |
| add a **workbook column** | `R/0-column_schema.R` | **not only there.** `switch_check()` fills defaults through 23 hand-written calls, not a loop, so a column with a default needs a 24th in `R/0-switches.R`; `meta = TRUE` is the constructor default and `R/data.R`'s `@format` is pinned to the schema by `test-schema-canonical.R`; and `meta_data_names.xlsx` is a committed file regenerated by `data-raw/regenerate_meta_xlsx.R`. `.claude/commands/new-column.md` has the full eight-step recipe |
| add a **switch value** (a new form name) | `R/0-switches.R` (the relevant `*_map`) | `validate_switches()` rejects anything not in the map |
| change **what a parameter starts at** | `R/2-build_params.R` | `R/4-build_parameter_bounds.R` if it needs bounds |
| change **which parameters are estimated** | `R/3-build_map.R` | `R/6-phaser.R` if it should be phased |
| add a **covariate or time-varying effect** to a process | `linkage_spec()` in `R/0-build_linkage.R` | the process's own `build_*()`. Nothing in the TMB template if the parameter already accepts a linkage; a **new parameter** needs `R/0-linkage_encode.R` and `src/TMB/linkage.hpp` changed in lockstep, and a **new process or link** must be added to `LINKAGE_PROCESSES_IMPLEMENTED` / `LINKAGE_LINKS_IMPLEMENTED` in `R/0-linkage_table.R` or it is refused as reserved |
| add a **data input** | `R/0-column_schema.R` + `R/0-read_write_excel_data.R` | `R/1-data_check.R`, `R/5-rearrange_data.R`, and the `DATA_*` block in `ceattle.cpp`. A `data_list` element with no read/write support round-trips to nothing |
| change a **reported quantity** | `REPORT()`/`ADREPORT()` in `ceattle.cpp` §14 | `R/6-rename_output.R` and `R/0-quantity_dictionary.R` |
| change **predation / suitability** | `src/TMB/predation.hpp` | `R/3-build_map.R` (`build_map_predation`), and run the hake MSE — `/golden-check` does not reach estimated suitability |
| change **growth or weight-at-age** | `src/TMB/growth.hpp` | `R/0-build_growth.R` |
| change a **reference point or the HCR** | `src/TMB/spr.hpp` and `ceattle.cpp` §6.2 for the SPR proxies; §6.6–6.7 for the depletion-based points and the projection HCR | `R/0-build_hcr.R`, and `build_hcr_map()` in the same file for its parameters |
| add a **plot** | `R/7-plot_helpers.R` for the shared resolvers, then the topical `R/7-plot_*.R` | `?"rceattle-plot-args"` documents the shared argument vocabulary once; `quantity_dictionary()` gives the axis label and units |
| add an **observation-error draw** | the `SIMULATE{}` block beside the density that scores it, in `ceattle.cpp` | `sim_mod()` implements no observation model in R; a new likelihood family owes a draw |
| change **projection or the MSE** | `R/10-run_mse.R` | `R/10-mse_summary.R`; anything touching row counts or draw order changes every subsequent random draw |

## The fit pipeline

`fit_mod()` (`R/6-fit_mod.R`) orchestrates the following stages. The
number-prefixed file names mirror this order.

| Stage | File | Function | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `R/0-clean_data.R` | `clean_data()` | Coerce and clean the incoming `data_list`. |
| 2 | `R/0-switches.R` | `switch_check()` | Fill missing switches with defaults; normalize string/integer switches. |
| 3 | `R/1-data_check.R` | `data_check()` | Validate inputs; error early on unsupported options. |
| 4 | `R/2-build_params.R` | `build_params()` | Build the starting parameter list from the switches. |
| 5 | `R/3-build_map.R` | `build_map()` | Build the TMB `map` (which parameters are estimated vs. fixed). |
| 6 | `R/4-build_parameter_bounds.R` | `build_bounds()` | Lower/upper parameter bounds. |
| 7 | `R/5-rearrange_data.R` | `rearrange_data()` | Reshape the data for TMB (and build the OSA observation vector when requested). |
| 8 | `R/6-fit_mod.R` | `fit_mod()` | `TMB::MakeADFun()` → `nlminb()` → `TMB::sdreport()`. |
| 9 | `R/6-rename_output.R` | `rename_output()` | Label derived quantities on the returned object. |

Phasing (optional staged estimation) is handled by `set_phases()` /
`TMBphase()` in `R/6-phaser.R`; `TMBAIC()` (`R/6-tmb_aic.R`) computes AIC.
Downstream wrappers (`retrospective()`, `jitter()`, `run_mse()`, `sim_mod()`,
`self_test()`, the `plot_*()` family) all take the fitted `Rceattle` object
returned by `fit_mod()`.

Before that pipeline runs, a user can assemble or edit the `data_list`
programmatically and see exactly what a given model needs, see
**Data assembly and the column schema** below.

## Every file in `R/`, and what it does

All 67, one row each, grouped by what they are *for* rather than by their number
prefix — the prefix tracks pipeline order only for the `1-` to `6-` chain, and
the 31 files under `0-` are shared machinery that the chain draws on. The nine
files a fit passes through are repeated here so this table is complete on its
own; [The fit pipeline](#the-fit-pipeline) gives them in order.

A note on vocabulary used below, because two words do double duty in this
package. **The map** means the TMB `map`, the mask saying which parameters are
estimated and which are held fixed; a parameter that is "mapped out" is not
estimated. A **switch map** (`sel_map`, `q_map`) is a different thing: a lookup
from the readable name a user types to the integer the template consumes.
**Deviates** are the annual offsets that make a parameter time-varying —
estimated per year, and penalized or integrated as random effects depending on
the setting. **Apical** selectivity is selectivity at the age or length where
the curve peaks.

**Specifications and registries** — the source of truth for what a setting
means. Change a value here and the rest of the package follows.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `0-column_schema.R` | **Every workbook column**: name, sheet, type, default, allowed values, old spellings, TMB target, and the one-line `doc` that is written verbatim into `meta_data_names.xlsx`. Note the `?BS2017SS` field text is *not* generated from it — that lives in `data.R` and is only asserted to agree. `has_default` is wired for `fleet_control` only; for the 34 control and bioenergetics scalars the `default` field is documentation. |
| `0-switches.R` | The 20 switch maps (`sel_map`, `q_map`, `initMode_map`, …) mapping a readable name to the template's integer, plus `switch_check()` / `validate_switches()` / `convert_switches()` / `revert_switches()`. Also the selectivity-penalty sign registry `.RCE_SEL_PEN_POSITIVE` and the `Sel_norm_bin` codes. `switch_check()` fills defaults through 23 hand-written calls, one per column — not a loop over the schema. |
| `0-parameter_dictionary.R` | Internal parameter name → natural-scale name, process, meaning, dimensions. Exported as `parameter_dictionary()`. |
| `0-parameter_index.R` | Parameter → model coordinate: which axes a block's dimensions mean (species, sex, fleet, year, age, bin), the slot labels for seven non-selectivity blocks *and* for each selectivity form, and the shortened-axis registry. Exported as `parameter_index()`. |
| `0-quantity_dictionary.R` | Reported quantity → meaning, **units**, dimensions. Exported as `quantity_dictionary()`. |
| `1-data_requirements.R` | `data_requirements()`: which inputs a given configuration requires, which are optional, which are ignored. |
| `1-data_requirements_table.R` | The requirement catalogue that function reads, plus the per-element classification helpers. |
| `data.R` | The `@format` field dictionary for the bundled datasets — hand-maintained, and pinned name-for-name against `0-column_schema.R`'s `doc` by `test-schema-canonical.R`. Adding a schema column with `meta = TRUE` and not updating this file is a CI failure. |

**Building a model specification** — the `build_*()` family, called before fitting.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `0-build_data.R` | `build_data()`: assemble or edit a `data_list` in R, supplying only the inputs a configuration uses. |
| `0-model_config.R` | `model_config()`: the model-level switch bundle, and its print method. |
| `0-build_srr.R` | The stock–recruit relationship: form, priors, fixed or estimated, and its linkages. |
| `0-build_m1.R` | Natural mortality `M1`: form, priors, linkages, and the retired-argument refusals. |
| `0-build_growth.R` | Growth form (von Bertalanffy, Richards), the population length grid, and growth linkages. |
| `0-build_selectivity.R` | Selectivity linkages, the apical-offset rows, and which forms accept which linkage. |
| `0-build_catchability.R` | Catchability linkages and the analytical-q forms. |
| `0-build_composition.R` | Composition weighting, including the Dirichlet-multinomial weight priors. |
| `0-build_hcr.R` | `build_hcr()`, the harvest control rule, and `build_hcr_map()`, which maps its parameters. |
| `0-fit_control.R` | The optimizer, `sdreport` and phasing knobs, bundled for `fit_mod()`. |
| `0-save_config.R` | `save_config()` / `load_config()` / `run_config()`: a run's whole configuration as commented YAML. |
| `0-priors.R` | `prior_normal()` and friends, for linkage coefficients. |

**The linkage system** — one formula grammar covering every way a parameter can
vary (covariate, time block, random effect), for every process.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `0-build_linkage.R` | `linkage_spec()`, the user entry point; materialization; the random-effect registry. The largest file in this subsystem. |
| `0-linkage_formula.R` | Splits a formula into its fixed and random parts. |
| `0-linkage_table.R` | The long-format coefficient registry every process writes into, and the refusals for a reserved-but-unwired process or link. |
| `0-linkage_encode.R` | Turns that table into the parallel vectors and the dense design matrix the template reads. Must stay in lockstep with `src/TMB/linkage.hpp`. |

**Reading and writing data.**

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `0-read_write_excel_data.R` | `read_data()`, `write_data()`, `write_template()` — the workbook round-trip, including the legacy sheet-name aliases. |
| `0-clean_data.R` | Coerce and tidy an incoming `data_list`; split the initial equilibrium catch out of `catch_data`. |
| `0-combine_data_sets.R` | `combine_data()`: merge two data lists. |

**The fit chain** — the nine stages `fit_mod()` runs, in order.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `1-data_check.R` | `data_check()`: validate the inputs and refuse unsupported combinations. Emits conditions only; returns nothing a fit reads. The per-form `Time_varying_sel` restrictions live here. |
| `2-build_params.R` | `build_params()`: the starting parameter list, and the linkage intercept initial values. |
| `3-build_map.R` | `build_map()`: the TMB map — which parameters are estimated and which are held fixed — assembled per process, plus the shared-parameter-block adjustment. |
| `4-build_parameter_bounds.R` | `build_bounds()`: lower and upper bounds, on the scale each parameter is stored on. |
| `5-rearrange_data.R` | `rearrange_data()`: reshape the data into the arrays the template expects, and build the OSA observation vector. |
| `6-fit_mod.R` | `fit_mod()`: the entry point. Assembles the TMB inputs, optimizes, projects under the HCR, and labels the output. |
| `6-phaser.R` | `set_phases()` / `TMBphase()`: ADMB-style phased estimation. |
| `6-rename_output.R` | `rename_output()`: labels every derived quantity, including the `jnll_comp` row names. Also holds the McAllister–Ianelli weight *calculation* (`calc_mcall_ianelli()`), which `6-reweight.R` iterates. |
| `0-tmb_helpers.R` | The `nlminb` + `sdreport` wrapper, the estimability check, and the marginal-gap diagnostic. |

| `6-tmb_aic.R` | `TMBAIC()`: marginal AIC. |

| `0-rceattle_class.R` | The nine S3 methods on a fit — `print`, `summary`, `plot`, `coef`, `vcov`, `logLik`, `residuals`, `as.data.frame`, `simulate` — and the Pearson residual machinery. |

### Three dictionaries you can just run

Worth knowing before reading any code: three of the registries above are
**exported functions**, and between them they answer "what is this variable and
what are its units" without opening the template.

```r
quantity_dictionary()   # reported quantity -> meaning, units, dimensions
parameter_dictionary()  # internal parameter name -> natural-scale name, process
parameter_index()       # parameter -> which axis each dimension means
```

Note the output names changed in the 5.x series: the quantities older scripts
and the wiki call `NByage` and `biomassSSB` are now `N_at_age` and `ssb`.
`quantity_dictionary()` is the authority on the current name.

## The switch system

Model options are supplied either as strings (`"Logistic"`, `"NPFMC"`) or as
the integer codes the TMB template consumes. `R/0-switches.R` is the single
source of truth for that correspondence, via four functions:

* `switch_check()`: fill missing switches with defaults and normalize.
* `validate_switches()`: error if any switch is not a known code/string.
* `convert_switches()`: canonical string → integer code for TMB.
* `revert_switches()`: integer code → canonical string (backward
  compatibility for older integer-coded data files).

The mappings live in named vectors: `sel_map`, `tv_sel_map`, `q_map`,
`tv_q_map`, `comp_loglike_map`, `fleet_map`, `initMode_map`, `suitMode_map`,
and `hcr_map`. Adding a value to a map is what makes a new string name legal;
`validate_switches()` rejects anything not listed.

## Data assembly and the column schema

A CEATTLE `data_list` has many possible inputs, but any one assessment uses only
some of them. A few pieces keep that manageable.

**The column schema (`R/0-column_schema.R`) defines every `fleet_control`
column in one place.** `.rce_column_schema()` records each column's name, type,
default value, older accepted spellings, and a one-line description. The rest of
the package reads the column from there, so adding a column means editing this
one file:

* `switch_check()` fills its default,
* `write_data()` writes it to the workbook and `read_data()` reads it back,
* the meta sheet and the `?BS2017SS` field descriptions document it,
* `data_check()` and `rearrange_data()` refer to it by its current name.

If a column has older accepted spellings, list them in the schema's `aliases`
field. Whenever a `data_list` enters the pipeline, an older spelling is
translated to the current name automatically, so workbooks and scripts written
against earlier column names keep working (`test-schema-canonical.R` checks this).

Both spellings at once is the case to know about, because it is what a script
produces when it assigns an older name to a `data_list` that `read_data()` has
already translated: the assignment creates the old column beside the new one.
They must then hold the same setting (an integer switch code and its string
count as the same) and anything else is an error naming both values. Nothing is
merged and no blank is filled in from the other column, because `NA` is a real
setting in several of these (`Sel_norm_bin` and `Sel_cap_bin` mean "do not
normalize" and "no cap"; `Proj_F_proportion` means "no F apportioned"), so
filling could not express clearing a value and would move a number silently.
Until 5.25.0 the older spelling was simply discarded here, which is how several
assessment scripts came to be running settings they did not ask for.

**`data_requirements()`** reports, for a given model setup, which inputs that
model requires, which are optional, and which are ignored, so you can see what a
configuration needs before fitting rather than hitting a validation error partway
through.

**`build_data()` with `model_config()`** assembles or edits a `data_list` in R,
supplying only the inputs a given model uses, and prints the model as a readable
outline (`print()` / `summary()`). `write_template()` writes a blank workbook
with the right sheets and columns for a chosen configuration.

## Run configuration (save / load)

`save_config()` and `load_config()` write and read a run's full configuration,
the model setup plus the estimation and uncertainty settings from
`fit_control()`, as a plain-text YAML file. Each field is commented with its
meaning, and fields left at their default are omitted, so two saved runs differ
in the file only where they differ in substance, and the file reviews cleanly in
version control.

Apply a saved configuration with
`fit_mod(data_list, config = load_config("run.yaml"))`. It fills in only the
arguments you did not pass yourself, so an explicit argument always takes
precedence. Every fit also stores the configuration it ran with, available as
`run_config(fit)`. Formulas, priors, and nested `build_*()` specifications all
save and reload, so reopening a saved configuration reproduces the same fit.

## The TMB template

`ceattle.cpp` includes these modules (order matches the top of the
file):

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `helper_functions.hpp` | Shared utilities. |
| `comp_osa.hpp` | Composition likelihoods and the one-step-ahead (OSA) decomposition. |
| `growth.hpp` | Growth (von Bertalanffy / Richards); weight- and length-at-age. |
| `selectivity.hpp` | Selectivity forms, dispatched by `switch (sel_case)` — `sel_case` is `Selectivity` unless form 13 is under a random walk, which rewrites it to `-13`: logistic (1), Ianelli non-parametric (2), double logistic (3), descending logistic (4), Hake/Taylor non-parametric (5), 2D/3D AR1 (6/7), double normal (8), NonParametricPM (9), LogisticPM (11), NonParametricIntegrable (13), DoubleNormalSS3 (15, Stock Synthesis size pattern 24, with its own `sel_dn6` parameter array). Codes 10, 12 and 14 are unused; the next free code is 16. |
| `recruitment.hpp` | Stock–recruitment functions. |
| `bioenergetics.hpp` | Temperature-dependent ration / consumption (`Ceq`). |
| `predation.hpp` | Prey suitability and predation mortality (MSVPA type-2, estimated iteratively). |
| `diet_data.hpp` | Predator diet (stomach-content) likelihood. |
| `linkage.hpp` | Applies the encoded linkage tables (covariates, time blocks, random effects) to each process's parameters, and accumulates the linkage priors / RE densities into the likelihood. |
| `comp_sim.hpp` | Composition draws: multinomial (sequential conditional binomial), Dirichlet, and Dirichlet-multinomial, used by the `SIMULATE` blocks. |

The model opens with the `DATA_*` block (switches such as `estimateMode`,
`msmMode`, `suitMode`, `initMode`, `srr_fun`, `HCR`, plus the data objects),
then the `PARAMETER_*` block, then the population and observation dynamics, and
finally the joint negative log-likelihood. The likelihood is accumulated in the
`jnll_comp` matrix, rows are likelihood components, columns are species/fleet.
Each row is addressed by a named constant from the `JnllRow` enum
(`JNLL_INDEX`, `JNLL_CATCH`, `JNLL_COMP`, … `JNLL_LINKAGE_RE`, with
`JNLL_N_ROWS` dimensioning the matrix), so a row is referred to by name in the
C++ rather than by a bare integer. The enum has **two hand-synced partners**:
the display names in `R/6-rename_output.R`, and `.JNLL_ROW_AXIS` in
`R/9-profile.R`, which records whether a row's columns count fleets or species.
Adding or reordering a row means updating all three by hand, or a row is
classified on the wrong axis and a survey's likelihood is reported against a
species. `tests/testthat/test-schema-jnll-rows.R` reads the template and asserts
the three agree.

**Building.** `src/TMB/compile.R` compiles the model (`framework = "TMBad"`);
`TMB` and `RcppEigen` are `LinkingTo` dependencies. The spurious Eigen
`-Warray-bounds` warnings are silenced by a source `#pragma` in the `.cpp`
rather than a compiler flag, since CRAN rejects warning-suppressing flags.

## The linkage and priors system

Every process's parameters share one formula-driven linkage system:
`R/0-build_linkage.R`, `R/0-linkage_encode.R`, `R/0-linkage_table.R`, and
`R/0-priors.R`. `linkage_spec(formula = ~ x, by = ~ ..., init = , priors = )` is
the user entry point, attached through the per-process builders:

* `build_srr()`: recruitment (`R0`, `alpha`, `beta`),
* `build_M1()`: natural mortality (`M1`),
* `build_growth()`: growth (`K`, `L1`, `Linf`, `m`) and the SD endpoints
  (`sd_L1`, `sd_Linf`),
* `build_catchability()`: catchability (`q`),
* `build_selectivity()`: selectivity (`slp_asc`, `slp_desc`, `inf_asc`,
  `inf_desc`, `coff`),
* `build_composition()`: the Dirichlet-multinomial weights (`theta_comp`,
  `theta_caal`, `theta_diet`), **prior-only**.

The same formula grammar covers every way a parameter can vary. The
right-hand side can be a covariate (`~ temp`), a set of time blocks
(`~ cut(Year, ...)` (the fixed part goes straight to `model.matrix()`, so
there is no bespoke block helper), or a year-to-year random effect) independent
(`~ (1|Year)`), a random walk (`rw(1|Year)`), or first-order autoregressive
(`ar1(1|Year)`). `~ 1` with a `priors` list leaves the parameter at one value but
places a prior on it. Use `by =` to say what the effect varies over,
`by = ~ species + sex + age_bin` for the population processes,
`by = ~ fleet` for catchability and selectivity.

Placing a **prior** on a selectivity, catchability, or composition-weight
parameter is the `~ 1` case, keyed by `` `(Intercept)` ``, e.g.

```r
build_selectivity(linkages = list(
  inf_asc = linkage_spec(~ 1, by = ~ fleet,
                         priors = list(`(Intercept)` = normal(50, 10)))))
```

The Dirichlet-multinomial composition weights take a prior only (they have no
covariate or random-effect form). See
`vignette("environmental-linkages-and-priors")` for the full grammar.

Note that inside `priors = `, the bare constructors `normal()`, `lognormal()`,
`gamma()`, `beta()` are **not** the exported `prior_*()` functions.
`linkage_spec()` evaluates the `priors` quosure in a data mask
(`rlang::eval_tidy(..., data = .prior_dispatch_mask())`) that binds
`normal` → `prior_normal`, and so on. Both spellings work inside
`linkage_spec()`, and the bare form is intentional, do not "fix" it to
`prior_normal()`.

## Recipes

### Add a new estimated parameter

1. Declare the `PARAMETER` in `ceattle.cpp` and use it in the relevant
   `.hpp` module.
2. Add a default starting value in `R/2-build_params.R`.
3. Add mapping logic in `R/3-build_map.R` (and the matching `build_map_*()`
   helper) so it is turned on/off for the right configurations.
4. Add it to the phasing order in `R/6-phaser.R`.
5. Add it to the parameter dictionary in `R/0-parameter_dictionary.R`. It is a
   registry keyed by parameter name, so a new (or retired) block that misses it
   fails only later.
6. If the parameter is a random effect, give it a `SIMULATE` draw beside its
   density (see *Change the likelihood*), or `sim_mod(process = )` will hand back
   its fitted values as though they were simulated.
7. (Optional) expose an on/off or random-effect switch as a `fit_mod()`
   argument.
8. Document it in `inst/extdata/meta_data_names.xlsx` and/or the `fit_mod()`
   roxygen.

### Add a new reported quantity

1. `REPORT()` it in `ceattle.cpp` (and `ADREPORT()` it if it needs a standard
   error). A `REPORT` inside a comment block is not reported, enumerate from a
   real fit, not from a grep, when checking what a model actually returns.
2. Give it dimension names in `R/6-rename_output.R` if it is an array.
3. Add it to the quantity dictionary in `R/0-quantity_dictionary.R`, with its
   units and whether it holds a standard error.
   `test-schema-quantity-dictionary.R` reads the template and a fit and asserts
   the two agree, so a quantity added here and not there fails a test.
4. If a quantity is only defined for some configurations, the per-recruit
   reference points are computed only under `msmMode = 0`, say so in its
   `meaning`, and gate it in `report_tables()`. CEATTLE leaves a *number* behind
   rather than a gap, so an ungated quantity reports a plausible wrong figure.

### Add or change a data input

There are two cases. Follow the one that matches.

**A `fleet_control` column** (e.g. a new per-fleet setting), add it in **one**
place, `R/0-column_schema.R`:

1. Add a row to `.rce_column_schema()` with the column's canonical name, type,
   default, any back-compat `aliases`, and its doc string. Everything downstream
   (`switch_check()` default-filling, `write_data()`/`read_data()` ordering, the
   meta sheet, the field dictionary) reads from the schema, so no other file needs
   editing to make the column persist and round-trip.
2. Consume the column where it matters (`data_check()`, `rearrange_data()`, or the
   cpp) by its **canonical** name, aliases are already upgraded on entry.
3. If it is a rename of an existing column, put the old spelling in `aliases` and
   pin it in `test-schema-canonical.R`.

**A whole new `data_list` element** (a new sheet / array, e.g. an index covariate):

1. Add the `DATA_*` object in `ceattle.cpp` and consume it in the module.
2. **Add read *and* write support in `R/0-read_write_excel_data.R`.** A new element
   with no `write_data()`/`read_data()` handling round-trips to nothing through the
   standard xlsx format; the feature is silently lossy. (This is exactly how
   `index_cov` was lost; it is the single most common data-input bug.)
3. Add validation in `R/1-data_check.R` and, if the model needs it, a row in the
   `data_requirements` table (`R/1-data_requirements_table.R`).
4. Add reshaping in `R/5-rearrange_data.R` if TMB needs a different layout.
5. Document it in `meta_data_names.xlsx` and/or roxygen.

### Add a new switch option (e.g. a selectivity form or `suitMode`)

For a selectivity form, [Adding a selectivity form](adding-a-selectivity-form.html)
traces one existing form through every file and names the tests that catch a
half-finished addition. The general shape:

1. Implement the case in the module `.hpp` (e.g. `selectivity.hpp` case *N*,
   `predation.hpp` `smode` *N*).
2. Register the string ↔ integer mapping in the relevant map in
   `R/0-switches.R` (e.g. `sel_map`, `suitMode_map`); otherwise
   `validate_switches()` rejects the new name.
3. If the option is not yet ready for use, block it in `R/1-data_check.R`, as
   the length-based suitability modes are (`suitMode %in% c(1, 3, 5)`).
4. Add bounds in `R/4-build_parameter_bounds.R` if the option introduces
   bounded parameters (see the `suitMode %in% c(1:2)` branch).
5. Add a test named `test-<area>-<topic>.R` in `tests/testthat/`.
6. Document it.

### Change the likelihood

The joint negative log-likelihood is assembled at the end of
`ceattle.cpp`, in the `jnll_comp` matrix, addressed by the `JnllRow` row
constant and the species/fleet column. Add or modify the relevant term there,
then recompile and re-run the regression tests (below) to confirm the objective
changes only as intended.

**Add or update the matching `SIMULATE` block at the same time.** Every
observation and every process error is drawn in a `SIMULATE` block next to the
density that scores it, so the two are edited together. A simulator that has
drifted from its likelihood does not error, it makes `self_test()` report
recovery against a data-generating process the model never assumed. Three rules
the existing blocks follow:

* **Draw what the density assumes**: including the bias-correction convention and
  the scale (log vs. natural). Where a family has no exact sampler (a
  multivariate normal truncated to the positive orthant, say) note it in the
  draw and warn from `sim_mod()` rather than substituting a different
  distribution.
* **Report under a `*_sim` name.** TMB never clears its report environment, so
  anything reported inside a `SIMULATE` block stays visible in `obj$report()`
  afterwards. A draw written into the observed-data object and reported under its
  name is readable as the data it replaced, which is why `comp_sim`, `caal_sim`
  and `diet_sim` are separate copies.
* **Do not draw what the model does not define.** If two densities score one
  latent, the AMAK/Ianelli stock-recruit penalty is the live example; there is
  no single distribution to draw from. Leave it and warn.

`simulate_state` selects which processes are redrawn (recruitment, M, growth,
catchability, selectivity). Its slot order is the linkage process code, so a
random linkage is gated by `simulate_state(linkage_process(i))` with no
translation, change one and change the other (`R/0-linkage_encode.R`).

`simulate_period` is a two-slot vector, and **only slot 0 is read**. It gates the
*process* draws, whose densities cover the hindcast alone. Observations are drawn
in every period deliberately, because `run_mse()` splices the negative-`Year` rows
back in as the next assessment's data, so gating them would hand the estimation
model observations that were never simulated. Slot 1 is reserved for a
projection-period process draw (WHAM uses its equivalent that way) and is inert
today; nothing in `sim_mod()`'s interface reaches either slot, and the tests and
`tools/verify/` scripts that exercise slot 0 do so through the internal
`.sim_draw(period = )`. Wiring slot 1 up means giving the projection-period
deviations a density to draw from first.

Both are `DATA_IVECTOR`s, defaulted in `build_osa_data()`, the single funnel
every data list passes through on its way to `MakeADFun()`.

## Testing

Tests use `testthat` in a flat layout: every file is a top-level
`test-<area>-<topic>.R` (for example `test-selectivity-logisticpm.R`,
`test-growth-sd-plus-group.R`, `test-likelihood-index-covariance.R`). Shared
`helpers-*.R` and `fixtures/` sit alongside them. Notable fixtures and guards:

* `tests/testthat/fixtures/fit_baseline.rds` and the golden-`jnll` regression
  test pin the objective-function value so unintended numerical changes surface.
* `test-tmb-makeadfun_smoke.R` checks the model builds and evaluates.
* `test-parameter-recovery.R` fits simulated data and checks estimates.
* `helpers-make-msm-data.R` builds small multi-species fixtures.

Run the suite with `devtools::test()` (or `testthat::test_local()`). After any
C++ change, recompile (`src/TMB/compile.R` or `pkgbuild::compile_dll()`) before
testing, since the tests load the compiled `.so`/`.dll`.

## Branches and releases

Feature branches are cut from `dev` and merged back into `dev`; the maintainer
merges `dev` into `main` as a release, following `inst/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`.
Operational assessments pin a tagged release. What a pull request holds
(`NEWS.md`, the `DESCRIPTION` version, the affected vignette), the commit-message
convention and what CI runs where are stated once, in
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/afsc-assessments/Rceattle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Debugging tips

* **`gradient is of length 1` (or similar).** The population is usually
  crashing, numbers-at-age going negative or a divide-by-zero. Check starting
  values and bounds for the offending process.
* **Model will not converge.** Inspect `mod$identified` (when reported) to see
  which parameters are hard to estimate, and adjust their starting values.
* **Reproducing an external model.** Supply numbers-at-age via the
  `NByageFixed` sheet and selectivity via `emp_sel` with `Selectivity = "Fixed"`,
  set `estDynamics = 1`, and run `fit_mod(estimateMode = 3)` to evaluate without
  re-fitting. (See also the [Stock Synthesis conversion](stock-synthesis-conversion.html)
  article.)

## The argument names, and what is deliberately left alone

The diagnostics take the fitted model as `object` (5.11.0). `Rceattle` and `fit`
still work and are silent; they warn from 5.12.0 and go in 6.0.0. To find your
own call sites now:

```r
options(Rceattle.warn_deprecated_args = TRUE)
```

Three keep their own names on purpose. `profile()` takes `fitted` because it is
an S3 method for `stats::profile()`, and renaming a method's first formal away
from its generic fails `R CMD check`. `mse_summary(mse = )` and
`compare_sim(operating_mod = )` take an MSE result and a set of simulations, not
a fitted model, so their names say more than `object` would.

The rest of the surface below is **known-awkward and deliberately unchanged**.
It is recorded here so it is not reopened each time someone reads the API cold.

*Switch codes are frozen.* Renumbering any of them silently reinterprets every
saved `run_config` YAML, every workbook, and every fitted `.rds` in
`../Rceattle-models` and `../GOA-ATF-ESP`, the same integer would mean
something new with nothing to signal it. This outweighs the readability of a
tidier numbering, so these stay as they are:

* `estimateMode` 0 = "Estimate" but 1 = "Hindcast", which reads backwards.
* `srr_fun`'s valid set is non-contiguous: 0/2/4 are live, 1/3/5 soft-deprecated.
* `sel_map` skips 10, 12 and 14.
* `initMode` 1 (`Equilibrium`) and 5 (`OffsetEquilibrium`) differ by one term.
* `msmMode` accepts 3–9, then `data_check()` rejects them.

*Overloaded columns.* `Time_varying_q` is a mode code for most fleets but a
1-based `env_data` column index (possibly comma-separated, `"1,3"`) when
`Catchability` is `Environmental` (5). Code 6 was the other such form and is
removed, but the overload is not academic: it is why the `Time_varying_q` mode
checks (`validate_switches()`, the soft-deprecation, and the 5.16.0 `"AR1"`
refusal) all exempt those fleets. A check that forgets it rejects a working
model for a value the assessor never set as a mode.

`Sel_curve_pen1` is a penalty weight for
selectivity 2/9/11/13 and `Sel_curve_pen2` a curvature penalty for 2/9/13, while
for 6/7 both are logit-scale AR1 correlations. Re-encoding either
would break existing workbooks; they are documented in the column schema
instead.

*Argument counts and names.* `fit_mod()` and `run_mse()` both take upwards of
twenty arguments, and the iteration counts are spelled `peels`, `njitter`,
`nsim` and `n_iter`, each idiomatic where it appears. `fit_mod()` also still
accepts the optimizer arguments that moved onto `fit_control()`, with a warning;
the live list is `.deprecated_ctl_args` in `R/6-fit_mod.R`.

*One more collision.* `compare_sim()` has an argument named `object` that is a
character selector for which part of the model to compare, not a fitted model.
It predates this release and is left alone for the same reason `operating_mod`
is, but it is the one place where `object` means something else.

*`profile()` is the odd diagnostic out.* It refits like `retrospective()`,
`jitter()` and `self_test()` but takes only a bare `getsd=`, no `phase`, no
`fit_control`, so every profile point refits at `.refit_like()`'s unphased
default. Worth knowing when reading a profile that looks flatter than expected.
